resources.string: See the motion you can\'t see.
Allow camera access to measure visual motion. If Android no longer asks, enable Camera in app settings.
No rear camera is available on this device.
Camera could not open. Check camera access and close other camera apps, then retry.
Frame analysis stopped. Retry the camera.
Use one black dot or square on white paper in good light. Keep it inside the center guide to acquire tracking, then move it slowly.
Displacement is from the first tracked position, in camera pixels. Losing the marker or restarting resets the reference. Keep the phone steady.
Start monitoring with a marker in view to see its motion graph.
Visual displacement over the last ten seconds in camera pixels. Gaps indicate lost tracking.
Tracking lost — gaps indicate unavailable readings.
SENSOR ERROR — stop and start to retry
The accelerometer measures the phone’s motion. Keep still briefly after starting. Peak resets each session; vibration thresholds are preliminary.
Monitoring uses both camera and accelerometer on every tab.
Open Visual to check camera access before starting.
g measures acceleration: 1 g ≈ 9.81 m/s². A still phone should settle near 0 g here because gravity is removed.
Includes gravity. These are phone sensor axes, separate from the marker’s X/Y position.

Based on RMS:
NORMAL: below %1$.2f g
VIBRATING: %1$.2f g to below %2$.2f g
HIGH: %2$.2f g or above
Prototype thresholds · uncalibrated, not safety limits.
g is acceleration relative to standard gravity, not grams. 1 g = 9.80665 m/s²; 0.10 g ≈ 0.98 m/s². It describes how quickly velocity changes, not distance or vibration frequency.

Distance from the first tracked marker position, measured in camera pixels (px), not screen pixels or millimeters. Losing the marker or restarting sets a new reference. Keep the phone steady: camera movement also changes this reading.
Marker coordinates in the full, unrotated camera image. These are absolute image positions, not movement amounts or phone sensor axes. Their directions may differ from the rotated preview.

Smoothed magnitude of the phone’s acceleration after estimated gravity is removed, in g. A still phone should settle near zero. This measures the phone’s motion; moving a remote object alone does not make the phone vibrate. Tilting the phone can briefly affect this reading.

Root mean square: the overall vibration level over the latest %1$.1f second(s), in g. Computed as the square root of the average squared, unsmoothed acceleration magnitudes after gravity removal. RMS drives the status label.

Highest smoothed magnitude since the session started or the analyzer reset, in g. The first %1$.1f seconds are excluded for warm-up. This is not the raw impact peak. RMS uses unsmoothed samples, so it can sometimes exceed this smoothed peak.

Measured in m/s², including gravity. In the phone’s natural portrait orientation: +X points right, +Y toward the top, +Z out of the screen. Axes stay fixed to the phone as the display rotates. Lying still face-up, values should be roughly X = 0, Y = 0, Z = +9.81 m/s².

Each shows the latest 10 seconds using its own timestamps. Visual history shows displacement in px; physical history shows smoothed acceleration in g. Vertical scales adjust automatically, so equal graph heights do not mean equal motion. Visual gaps indicate missing tracking; reacquisition starts from a new reference. Stop or backgrounding clears both histories. Frequency in Hz and distance in mm are not measured.

Sensor sampling requests %1$d Hz; the actual rate depends on the device. Physical readings refresh up to 10 times/second; visual readings up to 15. Gravity estimation uses a %2$.2f s filter time constant; magnitude smoothing uses %3$.2f s. Slow motion can be partly removed with gravity. A sensor gap longer than %4$.1f s or a backwards timestamp resets the analyzer, including peak. Restarting monitoring also resets it.
— means no valid reading is available. 0.00 is rounded to two decimal places and may include small motion or sensor noise. More decimal places do not imply calibrated accuracy.
